title: Rapid Handoff SOP for Multi-Region Incidents
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the rapid handoff and orchestration process for incidents that affect services across multiple regions (e.g., us-west + eu-central). It codifies timing expectations, handoff signals, decision ladders, runbook checkpoints, and customer-facing status templates so cross-region responders can coordinate with minimal overhead. Use this page as the canonical reference during multi-region degradations, full-region outages, and cross-region failovers.

Goals

- Restore customer-visible availability and reduce mean time to restore (MTTR).
- Ensure clear ownership for each affected service and geographic region.
- Avoid duplicated work and split-brain decision-making across regions.
- Provide consistent, timely customer communication from the earliest detection.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to any incident that meets one or more of the following: cross-region traffic routing issues, regional capacity loss, multi-region KV-store inconsistency, or simultaneous SLO regressions across regions.
- Not for single-service, single-region minor degradations where local runbooks and on-call ownership suffice.

Roles and responsibilities

- Bridge Operator (primary): owns the unified incident bridge, timeline, and public status page messages. Typically the on-call SRE for the primary impacted service.
- Regional Lead (one per affected region): coordinate triage and local mitigations in-region; report regional state to the bridge.
- Service Owner: technical owner for the product/service surface (model-serving, auth, routing, etc.). Responsible for action items and RCA.
- Escalation Liaison: senior eng/sre who facilitates cross-team decisions (fallbacks, cross-region failover approvals).
- Customer Comms Lead (CS/PR): drafts and approves external customer messages when severity > Sev2.

RTO / SLO thresholds and escalation triggers

- Sev1 (Full outage / widespread customer impact): any region with >= 50% reduction in successful request rate or latency > 5x baseline for 10+ minutes. Escalate to org-level bridge.
- Sev2 (Partial outage / degraded): user-facing errors or latency spikes affecting a subset of customers or routes. Requires cross-region check within 15 minutes.
- Escalate automatically to Escalation Liaison at T+30 minutes if mitigation unclear.

Rapid handoff timeline (T = detection time)

1) T+0 — Detect & Acknowledge (0–3 minutes)
   - Alerting system triggers cross-region page; first responder acknowledges in pager.
   - Bridge Operator creates/claims the incident bridge channel (Zoom/Slack bridge).
   - Post initial internal acknowledgement to status page: use template "initial_acknowledge" (see Customer comms).

2) T+3 — Bridge Formation & Roles (3–8 minutes)
   - Bridge Operator assigns Regional Leads and Service Owner in bridge.
   - Each Regional Lead posts current regional health summary: traffic, error rate, recent deployments.
   - If known, mark any automated failovers / scaling actions already executed.

3) T+8 — Rapid Triage (8–20 minutes)
   - Establish whether incident is a single-failure propagated via control plane (routing, DCS), or independent per-region failures.
   - If control-plane or shared dependency implicated, treat as unified incident and escalate to Org-level coordination.

4) T+20 — Decision Point (20–30 minutes)
   - Decide: (A) proceed with cross-region failover, (B) implement region-isolated mitigations, or (C) take a coordinated rollback.
   - Escalation Liaison must be involved for option A or C.

5) T+30+ — Stabilize & Handback (30 minutes onward)
   - Bridge Operator assigns post-stabilization owner and records action items.
   - If handing control back to regional ops, perform a formal Handoff Checklist (below).

Handoff Checklist (use before releasing bridge)

- Confirm observed customer impact and verify metrics baseline. (Bridge Operator)
- Confirm that all immediate mitigation actions are documented in the incident timeline. (Regional Leads)
- Validate that no outstanding cross-region decision remains (failover, rollback). (Escalation Liaison)
- Assign long-running action items with owners and due dates. (Service Owner)
- Schedule follow-up postmortem meeting within 48–72 hours. (Bridge Operator / Service Owner)

Decision ladder (who approves what)

- Local mitigations (scale, restart, config tweak): Regional Lead.
- Cross-region traffic shift / DNS failover: Escalation Liaison + Service Owner sign-off.
- Customer-impacting rollbacks: Service Owner + Product Manager + Escalation Liaison.

Bridge operator runbook quick commands

- Create bridge channel: /incident create --service=<service> --regions=us-west,eu-central --sev=1
- Attach runbook: /incident attach-runbook <runbook-id>
- Notify exec channel: /incident notify-exec --summary "Multi-region routing degradation"

Evidence collection checklist (must be captured in timeline)

1) Timeline entries for each action (timestamped): detection, ack, mitigations, role assignments.
2) Key system graphs: per-region request rate, error rate, P50/P95 latency, queue depth.
3) Recent deploys or infra changes in the prior 60 minutes.
4) Network/bgp/dns changes, cloud region health notices.

Customer communication templates

- initial_acknowledge (internal & status page)
  "We have detected an issue affecting [SERVICE] impacting traffic in multiple regions. Our engineers are investigating. We will provide an update within 15 minutes. (Incident ID: [INCIDENT_ID])"

- ongoing_update (public)
  "Update: We are investigating elevated errors/latency affecting [SERVICE] across [REGIONS]. Current mitigation: [ACTION]. Next update in 30 minutes or earlier if there is a change."

- mitigation_progress (public)
  "Update: We have implemented [MITIGATION] which has reduced error rates by ~[PERCENT]. We continue to monitor and will provide a status when the issue is fully resolved."

- resolved (public)
  "Resolved: The issue affecting [SERVICE] across [REGIONS] has been resolved at [TIME UTC]. Root cause: [SHORT RCA]. Customers may need to retry in-flight operations; none of the user data was lost. A postmortem will be posted within 72 hours."

Status page guidance

- Post the initial_acknowledge as soon as the bridge is created (T+0–3).
- For Sev1 incidents, use the public status page and include a severity tag and affected regions.
- Update cadence: 15 minutes for the first hour, then 30 minutes until resolved.

Postmortem rubric and template (to be completed within 72 hours)

- Title: [Service] — Multi-Region Incident — [Date]
- Summary: two-paragraph summary of what happened and customer impact.
- Timeline: annotated time-stamped actions (raw evidence snippets).
- Impact: affected customers, latency, error counts, duration.
- Root cause analysis: Causal chain and contributing factors.
- Corrective actions: prioritized list with owners and target dates (P0/P1/P2).
- Learnings and follow-ups: process changes, monitoring gaps.

Game day checklist for multi-region scenarios

- Pre-game: identify 2 services and mark Regions A/B as simulated failure targets. Ensure valid canary traffic generators.
- During game: practice bridge creation, assigning Regional Leads, and executing a DNS/traffic shift.
- Validate: status page templates, exec notifications, and customer comm approval flow.
- Post-game: generate a short retro and update this SOP with any gaps discovered.

Rotation and handoff best practices

- Handoffs should be intentional: 5–10 minute synchronous overlap for critical incidents.
- Use a "brief, readback" pattern: outgoing oncall states the current hypothesis, outstanding actions, and next expected check-in time. Incoming oncall reads back to confirm.
- Maintain up-to-date personal runbook links in the oncall profile card.

Failure modes and mitigation patterns (examples)

- Control-plane cascade: prioritize isolating shared control-plane services (config store, routing layer) and execute region-level circuit breakers.
- KV-store split-brain: suspend cross-region writes and promote read-only routing to healthy regions until reconciliation.
- Network blackhole in a region: shift traffic via CDN/origin routing and coordinate with cloud provider for region-level diagnostics.

Appendices

- Appendix A: Example Handoff Slack script
  "
  [OUTGOING] 14:35 UTC — Handoff to @incoming
  Hypothesis: routing control-plane N+1 failure in us-west causing 502s.
  Actions taken: scaled router pool x2, disabled canary config v42, started failover per runbook.
  Outstanding: DNS TTL propagation expected until 14:50 UTC.
  Next check-in: 14:40 UTC.
  [INCOMING] 14:36 UTC — Readback: Confirmed.
  "

- Appendix B: Quick approvals matrix (names and escalation phone numbers)
  "Service Owner: @svc-owner (pager)
  Escalation Liaison: @sre-lead (pager)
  Customer Comms Lead: cs-lead@example.com
  "

- Appendix C: Runbook links (insert canonical runbook links here)
  "Routing runbook: [link:routing-runbook]
  KV reconciliation: [link:kv-reconcile]"

Notes and governance

- This SOP is reviewed quarterly and after every Sev1 multi-region incident.
- Major changes (new failover strategy, DNS architecture changes) must be approved by the SRE leadership team and documented here.

Contact and escalation directory

- Bridge Operator rotation: see /oncall/rotations (internal link).
- To request an urgent cross-region test or game day, file an RFC in the #ops-scheduling channel.
